title: Follow a link
prompt: Ben's department_id is 1. Show the name of the department with that id. Replace the ___.
hints: The value to look up is 1.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE id = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE id = 2;

title: Everyone linked to a row
prompt: Show the name and department_id of the employees in department 2.
hints: Filter on the foreign key: department_id = 2.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, department_id FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, department_id FROM employees WHERE id = 2;
wrongSolutions.why: Filters on the employee's own id

title: Is it unique?
prompt: A primary key has no repeats. Check students by showing the row count as row_count and the number of different ids as unique_ids.
hints: COUNT(*) counts rows, and COUNT(DISTINCT id) counts different ids.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9);

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS unique_ids FROM students;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(DISTINCT year_group) AS unique_ids FROM students;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM students;

title: A customer's orders
prompt: Customer 1 is Priya. Show the id and order_date of her orders, using the customer_id foreign key.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE orders SET customer_id = 1 WHERE id = 6; UPDATE orders SET customer_id = 3 WHERE id = 1;

solutions: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE id = 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Filters on the order's own id

title: A broken link
prompt: Hugo's manager_id is 99, but no employee has that id. Show the name of anyone whose manager_id is 99.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 99 WHERE id = 7; UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 2 WHERE id = 8;

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE manager_id = 99;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE id = 99;
wrongSolutions.why: Looks for an employee whose own id is 99

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE manager_id = 1;
